clue.text: Social occasion at which tipping in, the main was dutifully observed

definitions.text: Social occasion at which tipping in, the main was dutifully observed

parts.words: Social occasion at which tipping in, the main was dutifully observed
parts.note: a social gathering where the ritual was tipping a drink's leaves into the sea (the main), done as a patriotic duty in 1773 Massachusetts

explanation.surface: An event where pouring something into the sea was carried out as a solemn duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tipping in the main' looks like serving at a dinner, but it means tipping chests of tea into the sea ('the main'), the 1773 protest by American colonists against British tax.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1773 protest is named as a kind of afternoon gathering, though its guests threw the refreshments into the harbour.

clue.text: Compound a poem about the team

indicators.note: about means the poem wraps around the team's letters

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: Someone composes verse about their sports side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' looks like a verb, but it is the chemistry noun; XI is the Roman eleven, the size of a cricket or football side.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxide is a chemical compound of oxygen with another element.

clue.text: It's drudgery to study the philosopher, nothing less

indicators.note: less means a letter for the word nothing is taken away from the run

parts.note: taken as written
to read a subject is to study it, as at a university
John Stuart Mill, the English philosopher
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Reading philosophy without a break is hard labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' removes the O (nothing) from TO, leaving T before READ and MILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is a byword for monotonous, wearying routine work.

clue.text: Attesting officer negatives a small railway

parts.note: not is the word of negation
RY is a short form of railway

explanation.surface: A certifying official vetoes a little railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A notary is a public official who witnesses and certifies documents.

clue.text: See 1
All the vessels suspended, being accident-prone

definitions.text: All the vessels suspended, being accident-prone

parts.words: All the vessels suspended, being accident-prone
parts.note: points to a counting song about glass containers hanging on a wall, one of which keeps accidentally falling

explanation.surface: A set of containers hanging up, all likely to come to grief.
explanation.walkthrough: The vessels are not ships but the glass bottles of the British children's counting song in which, verse by verse, one 'should accidentally fall' from the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's bottles hang on a wall and fall off one by one, each verse an accident.

clue.text: Deviate to get a rare beat .

indicators.note: to get here means to make or produce, so the letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A drummer told to stray from the rhythm to produce an unusual beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' signals the anagram: the letters of RARE BEAT rearrange to the answer. 'Deviate' also hints at the reshuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: To aberrate is to stray from the normal or right course.

clue.text: Make it snappy for an all-time record

definitions.text: Make it snappy for an all-time record

parts.words: Make it snappy for an all-time record
parts.note: snappy suggests snapshots, kept in a book of photographs, and a record suggests a long-playing disc

explanation.surface: A command to hurry in order to set a lasting record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make it snappy' sounds like 'hurry up', but snaps are photographs, and a photograph book is a permanent record; the word also means a music record.
explanation.definitionFit: An album holds snapshots as a lasting keepsake, and is also a long-playing record.

clue.text: Tense situation for one treading the straight, and narrow

definitions.text: Tense situation for one treading the straight, and narrow

parts.words: Tense situation for one treading the straight, and narrow
parts.note: describes a taut wire that a circus walker must follow in a straight narrow line, and the precarious situation it stands for

explanation.surface: Trying to live virtuously is a strain, as on the straight and narrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' means taut as well as anxious, and 'the straight and narrow' path of virtue becomes a literal straight, narrow wire under a circus performer's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A high wire is stretched taut and narrow, and the word is also an idiom for a delicate, risky situation.

clue.text: Girl allowed her aunt in Paris to be an art-lover.

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
let means allowed
tante is French for aunt

explanation.surface: A young woman's French aunt lets her become an art enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante is a dabbler and admirer of the arts, from the Italian for one who delights.

clue.text: Child claims the, luggage!

definitions.meaning: British children say '... I' to stake a claim to something first

explanation.surface: A child insists the suitcases belong to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags I!' is British schoolchildren's slang for claiming something first, so a child bags things.
explanation.definitionFit: A child stakes claims with the cry of the playground, and cases carried on a journey are also so named.

clue.text: What he offers is not so tough

definitions.meaning: a man who puts in a formal offer or bid
softer, as meat that is less chewy

explanation.surface: A man's bid is not driven hard.
explanation.walkthrough: A tender is a formal offer, so the man making it is one who tenders; the same letters are the comparative of tender, softer.
explanation.definitionFit: One who submits a formal bid is so named, and the comparative of soft-textured meat's adjective reads the same.

clue.text: ____ from towns he ran his godly race" (Goldsmith)

definitions.text: ____ from towns he ran his godly race" (Goldsmith)

parts.words: ____ from towns he ran his godly race" (Goldsmith)
parts.note: a line from Goldsmith's The Deserted Village describing the village preacher; the blank is the missing first word

explanation.surface: A quotation about a country parson living far from the town.
explanation.walkthrough: The line comes from Oliver Goldsmith's poem The Deserted Village (1770), about the village preacher who lived far from towns.
explanation.definitionFit: The parson lived distant from the towns, the sense the missing word gives.

clue.text: Stack of notes I made of the watercourse

parts.note: a wad is a thick bundle of banknotes

explanation.surface: Someone made a bundle of cash from a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A wadi is a dry riverbed in Arabia or North Africa that runs with water after rain.

clue.text: One leaves gin in the food, causing a row

indicators.note: in means the reduced gin goes inside the food

parts.note: aliment is a formal word for food or nourishment

indicators.note: leaves means the letter for one departs from gin

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone takes the gin out of the meal and causes an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One leaves gin' takes I from GIN, leaving GN, which goes 'in' ALIMENT after ALI. 'row' is a line, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: An alignment is an arrangement of things in a straight line.

clue.text: Revise rent 'and lose return from this floor

indicators.note: revise means the letters of rent are reworked into a new order
return means the word lose is read backwards

explanation.surface: A landlord is told to rework the rent and give up the income from a storey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revise' rearranges RENT to ENTR, and 'return' turns LOSE into ESOL; 'return' looks like income.
explanation.definitionFit: An entresol is a mezzanine, a low storey between the ground and first floors.

clue.text: Wrapped up in an unusually deep novel

indicators.note: unusually suggests the letters appear in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: A reader is engrossed in a novel of rare depth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges the letters of DEEP NOVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Enveloped means covered or enclosed completely, as by a wrapping.

clue.text: Forgives Jack when he does what you are trying to do!

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, abbreviated AB, able-bodied seaman

parts.words: does what you are trying to do
parts.note: the reader is attempting to work out the puzzle, which is solving it

explanation.surface: A sailor is pardoned when he gets the crossword out.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue addresses the solver: what you are trying to do is solve this clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve is to pardon or release from guilt.

clue.text: Rich dish makes ill a sailor in a U-boat

indicators.note: in means the sick sailor goes inside the submarine

parts.note: a U-boat is a German submarine, sub for short
taken as written
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A rich meal sickens a seaman aboard a submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: ILL and AB go 'in' SUB, after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sillabub is an old creamy dessert of whipped cream curdled with wine, a rich sweet.

clue.text: Contends with the last — of the levies.

indicators.note: the last part of the word levies is taken, its closing letters

explanation.surface: A tax collector struggles with the final batch of levies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last' of LEVIES is its closing four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To vie is to compete or strive with others.

clue.text: Stop these jokes

definitions.meaning: gaps in a wall that a filler plugs

explanation.surface: Someone telling a comedian to quit the gags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' means fill or plug, as with gaps in plaster, not 'cease'.
explanation.definitionFit: Splits in plaster are what a filler plugs, and quips are the same word.

clue.text: Not quite the most "in colour for a bow

definitions.text: Not quite the most "in colour for a bow

parts.words: Not quite the most "in colour for a bow
parts.note: the bow is a rainbow; the innermost band is violet, so the band just outside it is not quite the most inner

explanation.surface: A ribbon in a shade that is almost but not quite fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like fashionable, but means innermost, and 'bow' is a rainbow, whose innermost band is violet; the band next to it is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This deep blue lies between blue and violet in the spectrum, second from the inside of a rainbow.

clue.text: Not that Tennyson's poem was a pastoral one

definitions.text: Not that Tennyson's poem was a pastoral one

parts.words: Not that Tennyson's poem was a pastoral one
parts.note: Tennyson's Arthurian cycle carries this word in its title though it is not rustic, while the word properly means a short pastoral poem

explanation.surface: A remark that a famous Victorian poem was not really about country life.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's Idylls of the King are Arthurian tales, not rural verse, though the word in their title means a short poem of country life.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a short poem describing rustic life, as written by Theocritus.

clue.text: Beginner not well covered in a mountain region

parts.note: a tyro is a novice
lean means thin, without much flesh on the bones

explanation.surface: A thin novice climber in the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tyrol is an Alpine region of Austria and Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyrolean describes what belongs to or is found in the Tyrol, an Alpine area.

clue.text: It takes one on, when stage figures are checked

definitions.text: It takes one on, when stage figures are checked

parts.words: It takes one on, when stage figures are checked
parts.note: the word for checking accounts' figures, which takes on a letter for one plus the word on to become the trial of stage performers

explanation.surface: A tryout where theatre performers are vetted.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the inspection of accounts (figures checked); add I ('one') and ON and it becomes AUDITION, when stage performers are tested.
explanation.definitionFit: An audit is an official inspection of an organisation's accounts.

clue.text: Fresh from the wide Wyoming hills

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A breeze fresh from the wide open hills of Wyoming.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside wiDE WYoming, spanning the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Dewy means moist and fresh, as with morning dew.

clue.text: The old bone-shaker is a strangely-loved piece

indicators.note: strangely suggests the letters are in an odd arrangement

explanation.surface: An antique bicycle is a strangely cherished possession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges LOVED PIECE. A bone-shaker is an early bicycle with no rubber tyres.
explanation.definitionFit: The velocipede was an early pedal bicycle, nicknamed for its rough ride.

clue.text: Pen-catalogues of distinctive writers

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
lists are catalogues

explanation.surface: Catalogues of fountain pens by writers with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing tool, but it is an animal enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylists are writers admired for their style.

clue.text: Teased confoundedly, but remained composed

indicators.note: confoundedly suggests the letters are thrown into confusion

explanation.surface: Someone was teased mercilessly but kept calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confoundedly' rearranges TEASED.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means calm and unhurried in manner.
